evidence.note: A question about three World of Warships battleships weighs theoretical performance against the cost of building such large ships.

segments.summary: A question about three World of Warships battleships weighs theoretical performance against the cost of building such large ships.
segments.question: Could the World of Warships battleships Devastation, Maine and Cristoforo Colombo reach 30 knots in real life given their hull form, weight and topweight?
segments.answerShort: In theory, yes. Several smaller ships with most of the capability could be more attractive at comparable effort.

segments.title: Why the operation provides AI destroyers
segments.body: The operation can require torpedo hits for an extra objective. The players explain that a team could otherwise enter with no torpedo-equipped ships. AI destroyers ensure the scenario starts with that capability available. Losing those ships does not itself end the operation.

evidence.note: The operation supplies destroyers because the team might lack torpedoes for an optional objective.
The reply distinguishes losing the AI ships from failing the operation.

segments.summary: An optional torpedo objective explains why World of Warships supplies destroyers to a force that might have brought none.
segments.question: What happens if the team loses all of its AI destroyers?
segments.answerShort: The loss does not itself fail the operation. The destroyers are provided because the team might otherwise have no torpedoes for an optional objective.

segments.title: Algérie and Émile Bertin
segments.body: Algérie comes up as a ship even a critic of French cruiser design is willing to acknowledge. The reply challenges the idea that it was an exception by bringing in Émile Bertin as a second example.

evidence.note: Two French cruisers test a blanket judgment about how well France designed them.

segments.summary: Two French cruisers test a blanket judgment about how well France designed them.

segments.title: Rodney, Nelson and Collingwood in World of Warships
segments.body: In World of Warships, Rodney carries 24.5-inch torpedoes and receives a speed boost. Nelson has no torpedoes in the game. Collingwood also lacks them and is described as carrying three twin 16.5-inch mounts. The ships illustrate how the game gives each model a distinct set of capabilities.

evidence.note: The game gives Rodney torpedoes that its versions of Nelson and Collingwood lack, while Collingwood carries a different main battery.

segments.summary: The game gives Rodney torpedoes that its versions of Nelson and Collingwood lack, while Collingwood carries a different main battery.

segments.title: Glenn's favourite ship from 1905 to 1955
segments.body: The audience question asks Glenn to make the same choice the rest of the panel has already made. After hesitating, he settles on Renown as his probable favourite.

evidence.note: Glenn tentatively picks the battlecruiser HMS Renown when asked for a favourite ship from 1905 to 1955.

segments.summary: Glenn tentatively picks the battlecruiser HMS Renown when asked for a favourite ship from 1905 to 1955.
segments.question: What is Glenn's favourite ship of the period from 1905 to 1955?
segments.answerShort: His tentative choice is HMS Renown.

segments.title: Horseback archery among Mongolian students
segments.body: A greeting to a viewer in Mongolia leads to a recollection of teaching Mongolian students at Kingston. The students showed photographs of themselves shooting bows from horseback. Seeing the practice repeatedly changed the teacher's expectations about how common it was among that group.

evidence.note: A Kingston teaching anecdote gives a glimpse of horseback archery as a living practice.

segments.summary: A Kingston teaching anecdote gives a glimpse of horseback archery as a living practice.

segments.title: The navigation examination room at Greenwich
segments.body: A room under consideration for the Greenwich conference once hosted naval officers' navigation examinations. One proposal is to put the officers' lectures in that room. Another participant suggests asking a surprise navigation question for the occasion, an idea the organizer declines.

evidence.note: A former navigation examination room is proposed as the venue for naval officers' conference talks.

segments.summary: A former navigation examination room is proposed as the venue for naval officers' conference talks.
segments.question: Should the naval officers' talks at the Greenwich conference take place in the room once used for their navigation exams?
segments.answerShort: The panel sees no problem with the room and jokes about adding a navigation question. The organizer decides against the extra test.

segments.title: Playing Japan's army, navy and government separately
segments.body: The organizers describe a customized scenario in which the Imperial Japanese Navy and Army get different players. The civilian government and the emperor also have separate roles. With each player making decisions for a different institution, the participants expect infighting within Japan. The organizers are describing the setup for a planned role-playing session.

evidence.note: A Hearts of Iron IV scenario assigns separate players to Japanese institutions, making rival priorities part of the game.

segments.summary: A Hearts of Iron IV scenario assigns separate players to Japanese institutions, making rival priorities part of the game.

segments.title: The World War II counterpart to a galley
segments.body: The question looks for a World War II counterpart to a much older kind of warship. The motor torpedo boat is proposed because the comparison stresses closing with an enemy to fight at short range. The questioner points out that galleys were fully fledged warships in their own era. The reply treats the comparison as one of role and suggests that a larger ancient oared warship would warrant comparison with a capital ship.

evidence.note: A comparison with a motor torpedo boat rests on how a galley fights at close quarters.

segments.summary: A comparison with a motor torpedo boat rests on how a galley fights at close quarters.
segments.question: Which World War II vessel comes closest to the galley?
segments.answerShort: A motor torpedo boat is the proposed match if the comparison is about close-range fighting.

segments.title: Galleasses as fire-support ships at Lepanto
segments.body: The gun-armed ships in the comparison are the galleasses at Lepanto. They are described as fire-support ships, which prompts a tentative comparison with destroyers. The ordinary galley remains the example of a vessel that closes to fight.

evidence.note: At Lepanto, the galleass offers a different comparison with World War II ships because its role depended on its guns.

segments.summary: At Lepanto, the galleass offers a different comparison with World War II ships because its role depended on its guns.
segments.question: How does the comparison change for the gun-armed vessels at Lepanto?
segments.answerShort: Those vessels were galleasses, described here as fire-support ships. Their role prompted a tentative comparison with destroyers.

segments.title: Centreline and broadside torpedo launchers
segments.body: A player comes out of a destroyer encounter remembering that this ship carries centreline torpedo tubes. The expectation of a second set came from the separate port and starboard launchers on several American ships encountered in the game. A centreline mount can train toward either side. Separate banks give each side launchers of its own.

evidence.note: A World of Warships encounter illustrates the difference between a centreline mount and separate launchers on each side.

segments.summary: A World of Warships encounter illustrates the difference between a centreline mount and separate launchers on each side.

segments.title: Light cruiser armour and destroyer gunfire
segments.body: An early Condottieri cruiser prompts a discussion of very light belt protection in the game. Even a destroyer's guns can threaten it under those conditions. The comparison broadens to other cruisers, for which a close-range encounter can also change the usefulness of armour-piercing shells. The exchange concerns the game's protection and damage model.

evidence.note: The early Condottieri cruisers illustrate how thin protection changes a matchup between a destroyer and a light cruiser in World of Warships.

segments.summary: The early Condottieri cruisers illustrate how thin protection changes a matchup between a destroyer and a light cruiser in World of Warships.

segments.title: USS Massachusetts and the value of secondary guns
segments.body: Being surrounded by destroyers is a bad position for the ship on screen. A battleship with a substantial secondary battery can fare differently in World of Warships, and Massachusetts is the example the group picks. Its in-game reputation made it a frequent recommendation at its tier.

evidence.note: Massachusetts illustrates why a battleship's secondary battery changes a close encounter with destroyers in World of Warships.

segments.summary: Massachusetts illustrates why a battleship's secondary battery changes a close encounter with destroyers in World of Warships.

segments.title: HMS Aurora becomes the Chinese cruiser Chongqing
segments.body: The game's Chinese cruiser is identified as the former HMS Aurora. After transfer to the Republic of China it carried the name Chongqing. Its crew defected to the Communists on 25 February 1949, placing a former Royal Navy cruiser on the other side of the Chinese Civil War. The account mentions several later names for the same hull.

evidence.note: A question about the Chinese cruiser in World of Warships leads to the history of HMS Aurora and its crew's defection in 1949.

segments.summary: A question about the Chinese cruiser in World of Warships leads to the history of HMS Aurora and its crew's defection in 1949.
segments.question: Which real ship was the Chinese cruiser based on?
segments.answerShort: It was formerly HMS Aurora, transferred to the Republic of China as Chongqing before its crew defected to the Communists on 25 February 1949.

segments.title: Air attack and salvage of Chongqing
segments.body: The follow-up concerns the ship's fortunes after its change of allegiance. The answer recalls air attack, sinking and subsequent recovery. The exchange leaves the chronology and number of sinkings uncertain.

evidence.note: A follow-up question turns from Chongqing's defection to the loss and recovery of the former Royal Navy cruiser.

segments.summary: A follow-up question turns from Chongqing's defection to the loss and recovery of the former Royal Navy cruiser.
segments.question: What happened to Chongqing after the defection?
segments.answerShort: The discussion recalls air attack followed by loss and recovery of the hull, with the details of the sequence left uncertain.

segments.title: Chongqing and the loss of Soviet refit support
segments.body: The group links the end of the cruiser's prospects for modernisation to the Sino-Soviet split. The account describes a proposed Soviet-assisted overhaul that fell through as relations deteriorated. Conversion into a salvage ship was another proposal. Both ideas stayed on paper in the account given here.

evidence.note: The Sino-Soviet split comes up as a possible explanation for why a plan to modernise the former HMS Aurora fell through.

segments.summary: The Sino-Soviet split comes up as a possible explanation for why a plan to modernise the former HMS Aurora fell through.

segments.title: Aft gun mounts on Chongqing
segments.body: The unusual grouping would put all four twin mounts in the same part of the ship. The players question the arrangement after discussing a Soviet-backed overhaul that fell through. The exchange leaves it unclear whether the layout belongs to the game or a historical proposal.

evidence.note: A suggestion to group four twin 100 mm mounts aft prompts a brief exchange about the cruiser's gun layout.

segments.summary: A suggestion to group four twin 100 mm mounts aft prompts a brief exchange about the cruiser's gun layout.

segments.title: Reading shell impacts in World of Warships
segments.body: The hit indicators describe what the game says happened to shells that struck the target. A hit can penetrate the armour, fail to penetrate it or glance off. Multiple penetrations can register during one salvo. The hit count and damage total therefore tell the player different things.

evidence.note: Hit indicators distinguish penetration, failure to penetrate and ricochet, even when the ship's health bar hardly changes.

segments.summary: Hit indicators distinguish penetration, failure to penetrate and ricochet, even when the ship's health bar hardly changes.
segments.question: What shows whether shells are hitting effectively, apart from the target's health bar?
segments.answerShort: The hit indicators report penetrations, non-penetrations and ricochets, and show how many shells produced each result.

segments.title: An O'Neill cylinder in Exodus Gambit
segments.body: The author recalls the gateway station from Exodus Gambit as a large O'Neill cylinder. The description identifies its type of space habitat even though he cannot recall the station's formal name.

evidence.note: Asked to pick a space station from his books, the author chooses the gateway station from Exodus Gambit.

segments.summary: Asked to pick a space station from his books, the author chooses the gateway station from Exodus Gambit.
segments.question: Which space station from his books would the author pick?
segments.answerShort: His choice is the gateway station from Exodus Gambit, which he describes as a large O'Neill cylinder.

segments.title: Food in space and livestock in low gravity
segments.body: The author first wonders whether there would be food unique to space. The group considers whether beef raised on an asteroid might differ from beef raised on the ground. They float different ideas about what lower gravity would do to muscle and fat. The exchange leaves both the physiology and the taste open.

evidence.note: A question about a favourite space food turns into a thought experiment about cattle raised on an asteroid.

segments.summary: A question about a favourite space food turns into a thought experiment about cattle raised on an asteroid.
segments.question: What food from space would the author want to eat?
segments.answerShort: He gives no particular choice and wonders what food would be unique to space. The group speculates about how low gravity could affect livestock.

segments.title: Choosing HMS Tiger or HMS Lion for a wartime command
segments.body: The prompt asks each player to pick a First or Second World War ship they would want to command in combat. HMS Tiger is the first choice in the exchange. HMS Lion is another, complete with a joke about its name. The replies express affection for individual ships and give little operational rationale.

evidence.note: An audience question about commanding a ship from either world war elicits two British battlecruiser picks.

segments.summary: An audience question about commanding a ship from either world war elicits two British battlecruiser picks.
segments.question: Which First or Second World War ship would the players want to command in combat?
segments.answerShort: HMS Tiger and HMS Lion are the picks in this exchange. Personal preference and a play on Lion's name supply the reasons given.

segments.title: Why is the disabled carrier alone in Raptor Rescue?
segments.body: The carrier in the scenario is immobilised and apparently has lost its aircraft and ammunition. That leaves the group asking why a carrier would be alone and why its own escorts could not provide help. They consider whether the escorts were sunk or drew enemy ships away to buy time. The fictional setup makes the normal expectation of an escort screen explicit.

evidence.note: A World of Warships rescue mission raises the question of what a damaged carrier's escorts should be doing.

segments.summary: A World of Warships rescue mission raises the question of what a damaged carrier's escorts should be doing.
segments.question: Why is the carrier stranded ahead of the rescuing force?
segments.answerShort: The scenario gives the carrier damaged engines and depleted aircraft and ammunition. The group speculates that its escorts were sunk or went to draw off the enemy.

segments.title: A torpedo hit on the carrier's support ship
segments.body: A player spots a badly damaged merchant ship in front of the force and asks what happened. Another confirms a torpedo hit. They realise that losing the ship at that moment could cost them the operation. It is a game example of how a rescue mission can depend on protecting the vessels that make recovery possible.

evidence.note: Damage to a merchant ship exposes how the Raptor Rescue scenario depends on an auxiliary as well as on the carrier.

segments.summary: Damage to a merchant ship exposes how the Raptor Rescue scenario depends on an auxiliary as well as on the carrier.
segments.question: What happened to the merchant ship supporting the carrier rescue?
segments.answerShort: It took a torpedo hit. Its low remaining health put the operation at risk because the support ship was still needed.

segments.title: Anshan's gunboat role and torpedo trade-offs
segments.body: The players describe their destroyer as a gunboat and discuss its very short-range torpedoes. A different torpedo option offers greater reach at a lower speed. Those are choices in the game. The limited reach explains why the player is advised to rely mainly on the guns.

evidence.note: A Chinese destroyer illustrates how World of Warships assigns useful gun power to a ship whose torpedo options trade reach for speed.

segments.summary: A Chinese destroyer illustrates how World of Warships assigns useful gun power to a ship whose torpedo options trade reach for speed.

segments.title: The escort carrier's replacement aircraft
segments.body: A player expects the escort carrier accompanying the group to take an active part in the operation. The explanation offered is that it has already transferred its air group to the damaged carrier. The players also recall limits on what the escort carrier model could do in the original mission.

evidence.note: An apparently inactive escort carrier prompts a question about where its aircraft went in Raptor Rescue.

segments.summary: An apparently inactive escort carrier prompts a question about where its aircraft went in Raptor Rescue.
segments.question: Why isn't the escort carrier operating aircraft during the rescue?
segments.answerShort: In the mission explanation it has already transferred its aircraft to the damaged carrier. The players also recall that its original game model was limited.

segments.title: HMS Black Swan and early-tier damage rules
segments.body: Moving from Black Swan to Medea makes the speed difference immediately noticeable to the player. Black Swan is remembered as particularly strong in an earlier version of the game. At the time, low-tier ships had vulnerable citadel areas, and Black Swan could fire armour-piercing shells with a short reload. Those rules amplified the value of its armament.

evidence.note: A change from Black Swan to Medea leads to a recollection of what made Black Swan unusually effective at the first tier of World of Warships.

segments.summary: A change from Black Swan to Medea leads to a recollection of what made Black Swan unusually effective at the first tier of World of Warships.

segments.title: Armour-piercing shell fuzes and overpenetration
segments.body: A salvo produces overpenetrations, prompting a comparison of armour-piercing and high-explosive ammunition in the game. The players then describe an armour-piercing hit that reaches and detonates in a cruiser's machinery spaces. In this damage model a shell can pass through without detonating. Which damage result the game registers depends on what happens inside the ship.

evidence.note: An overpenetration in World of Warships illustrates why the same shell can have different effects on different parts of a ship.

segments.summary: An overpenetration in World of Warships illustrates why the same shell can have different effects on different parts of a ship.

segments.title: Hood's loss and magazine detonations in World of Warships
segments.body: The players use Hood to illustrate a difference between historical losses and the rules of the game. They say World of Warships removed magazine detonations as an instant-loss mechanic. For a player, the objection was that a random outcome could end a match without warning. Hood's catastrophic loss is the historical reference behind the joke.

evidence.note: A joke about repeating Hood's historical fate leads to a discussion of why World of Warships removed sudden detonations.

segments.summary: A joke about repeating Hood's historical fate leads to a discussion of why World of Warships removed sudden detonations.

segments.title: USS Massachusetts and the South Dakota class
segments.body: The Massachusetts in this match represents a real US Navy battleship. The initial answer establishes that the game uses the historical ship as its basis. When the question returns to the class, the group identifies it tentatively as South Dakota.

evidence.note: The group identifies the historical battleship represented by Massachusetts and recalls its class.

segments.summary: The group identifies the historical battleship represented by Massachusetts and recalls its class.
segments.question: What historical battleship does Massachusetts represent, and what class was she?
segments.answerShort: The game ship represents USS Massachusetts, which the group identifies as a South Dakota-class battleship.

segments.title: Tribal-class destroyer speed in the game and in service
segments.body: One player finds the Tribal destroyers slow in World of Warships. The reply recalls crews pushing real Tribals beyond their intended speeds and causing machinery trouble. The anecdote concerns the strain on machinery when crews demanded more speed, a different issue from how fast the simulated destroyers feel.

evidence.note: A complaint about slow Tribals in World of Warships prompts a comparison with reports of their machinery being pushed too hard in service.

segments.summary: A complaint about slow Tribals in World of Warships prompts a comparison with reports of their machinery being pushed too hard in service.

segments.title: The hull behind Weimar in World of Warships
segments.body: One player asks whether Weimar is built on Nürnberg's hull. The response points instead to Yorck, described here as a First World War cruiser. The speakers are identifying a design in the game, where a rendered ship and the historical names used to explain it can have different origins. The exchange gives a suggested identification and no plans or dimensions to compare.

evidence.note: A question about Nürnberg leads to a different proposed reference for Weimar's game hull, the First World War cruiser Yorck.

segments.summary: A question about Nürnberg leads to a different proposed reference for Weimar's game hull, the First World War cruiser Yorck.
segments.question: Is the World of Warships cruiser Weimar based on Nürnberg's hull?
segments.answerShort: A player suggests Yorck, a First World War cruiser, as the hull reference.

segments.title: A Tribal-class destroyer and the obstructions at Narvik
segments.body: In this account, a Tribal-class destroyer forced her way past ships sunk to obstruct the harbour. She is said to have come up on a partly submerged merchant vessel while engaging targets in the harbour. She was reportedly back in service soon afterward. No repair interval or damage survey is given.

evidence.note: The group recalls a Tribal-class destroyer navigating obstructions at Narvik.
The reply recalls a quick return to service and gives no damage estimate.

segments.summary: A question about damage at Narvik prompts an account of a Tribal destroyer crossing sunken blockships and returning to service.
segments.question: How badly was the Tribal destroyer damaged at Narvik when she pushed through the harbour obstructions?
segments.answerShort: The destroyer reportedly returned to service soon afterward. The exchange gives no specific damage or repair figures.

segments.title: Merchant-ship speed and repairs in a game convoy
segments.body: Closing on the freighter restores the player's ship in this World of Warships operation. Staying beside it proves surprisingly difficult. One player says the merchant ships are pulling away even with the destroyer showing 37 knots. The ensuing jokes about engineers exceeding their limits concern the behaviour of the simulated convoy.

evidence.note: A convoy freighter repairs nearby escorts and appears to pull away from a destroyer whose speed reads 37 knots.

segments.summary: A convoy freighter repairs nearby escorts and appears to pull away from a destroyer whose speed reads 37 knots.
segments.question: Does sailing close to the convoy freighter restore health in this operation?
segments.answerShort: Yes. The freighter restores health nearby, although its speed makes it difficult for the destroyer to stay close.

segments.title: Cossack's aggression and staying power in World of Warships
segments.body: Cossack is described as a ship that encourages aggressive play. The group sees a mismatch between the pressure she can put on opposing destroyers and her chances of surviving the exchange. A player who survives can stay in the match to harass cruisers from smoke. The tradeoff concerns how Cossack plays in World of Warships.

evidence.note: The players use Cossack to discuss why a destroyer that excels at pushing into an engagement can be hard to keep alive.

segments.summary: The players use Cossack to discuss why a destroyer that excels at pushing into an engagement can be hard to keep alive.

segments.title: Fleet of Fog Takao and its fictional armament
segments.body: Asked what just passed, one player identifies the heavy cruiser as Fleet of Fog Takao. The group explains the bright paint by joking that the fictional ships have little reason to hide. Their setting gives them exotic guns, corrosive torpedoes and energy shields. That combination belongs to the fictional fleet appearing in the game.

evidence.note: The bright cruiser passing the group turns out to be Fleet of Fog Takao, prompting an explanation of its appearance and fictional systems.

segments.summary: The bright cruiser passing the group turns out to be Fleet of Fog Takao, prompting an explanation of its appearance and fictional systems.
segments.question: What is the brightly coloured heavy cruiser that passes the group?
segments.answerShort: A player recognizes it as the Fleet of Fog heavy cruiser Takao.

segments.title: Who can clear the minefield in the escort game?
segments.body: The appearance of a minefield prompts a request for help. The player in a Tribal-class destroyer questions assigning the job to that ship. The group weighs the equipment currently available and considers another ship's depth-charge ability. The exchange concerns the tools the game gives the escort force.

evidence.note: The team considers which of its ships has a way to deal with a new obstacle without leaving the convoy unprotected.

segments.summary: The team considers which of its ships has a way to deal with a new obstacle without leaving the convoy unprotected.
segments.question: Does the Tribal-class destroyer have to clear the minefield?
segments.answerShort: It is considered because the team's options are limited. Another player thinks a depth-charge ability may offer an alternative.

segments.title: Depth charges and mines in a World of Warships escort
segments.body: A player credits in-game depth-charge air strikes with clearing the scenario's minefields. That result prompts a question about whether depth charges could clear a minefield more generally. The reply is brief and suggests a possibility. The group gives no example of a historical clearance operation.

evidence.note: A report of mine clearance in the game leads to a brief question about a real counterpart.

segments.summary: After the scenario's minefields are cleared, the group considers whether the game mechanic has a real counterpart.
segments.question: Could depth charges also clear a minefield outside the game?
segments.answerShort: The reply suggests a possible effect and gives no example of actual mine clearance.

segments.title: The convoy escort's transport-survival objective
segments.body: The operation requires the players to escort transports out of the zone. A single transport reaching the exit satisfies the condition. The group is told to expect another German attack while the transports are still exposed. This is the scenario's victory rule and explains why protecting the merchants takes priority here.

evidence.note: A question about which ships to protect clarifies how the operation judges convoy survival.

segments.summary: A question about which ships to protect clarifies how the operation judges convoy survival.
segments.question: Do the players need to protect the transports?
segments.answerShort: Yes. At least one has to leave the zone.

segments.title: High explosive and armour piercing in the escort scenario
segments.body: One player asks whether high explosive would be the simpler choice against the remaining ships. Another expects armour-piercing shells to deal much more damage when the game registers a good hit. Destroyers and secondary batteries qualify that advice. The comparison concerns the game's model of shell damage and the targets in this operation.

evidence.note: Players compare armour-piercing and high-explosive shell effects as the escort scenario enters its last fight.

segments.summary: Players compare armour-piercing and high-explosive shell effects as the escort scenario enters its last fight.
segments.question: Would high-explosive shells work better against the remaining ships in this operation?
segments.answerShort: The reply favours armour piercing when the game registers effective hits and makes an exception for destroyers.

segments.title: Keeping Hood at a distance in the escort scenario
segments.body: The player in Hood parks away from the immediate action and waits for destroyers to enter range. The group is fighting in a destroyer-heavy scenario with Hood modelled at tier VII. The player calls out the gap between this convenient game position and an actual battle. It is an example of how a fixed scenario lets a battlecruiser take a limited role alongside other players.

evidence.note: Hood remains at range while destroyers approach, illustrating a choice made possible by the scenario.

segments.summary: Hood remains at range while destroyers approach, illustrating a choice made possible by the scenario.

segments.title: Camouflage and trials paint in World of Warships
segments.body: Blue Archive camouflage changes how a ship looks. The players say binding it makes it permanent and leaves capabilities the same. They compare the camouflage on Queen Elizabeth with a two-tone pattern they describe as trials paint on Rooke. The schemes matter to them as visual choices in the game.

evidence.note: A question about Blue Archive camouflage leads to a comparison of the game's cosmetic paint schemes for British ships.

segments.summary: A question about Blue Archive camouflage leads to a comparison of the game's cosmetic paint schemes for British ships.
segments.question: Does Blue Archive camouflage change how the ship performs?
segments.answerShort: It is decorative only. The group says it cannot be unbound once it is applied to a ship.

segments.title: Main and secondary armament on Queen Elizabeth in World of Warships
segments.body: The choice in World of Warships is between upgrades for the main battery and the auxiliary armament. The recommendation is to favour the main battery because Queen Elizabeth's secondaries contribute relatively little in the game. The player values them for protection from aircraft and destroyers. The reply singles out weak secondary performance against destroyers on this ship.

evidence.note: The group weighs a main armament upgrade against relying more heavily on Queen Elizabeth's secondary weapons.

segments.summary: The group weighs a main armament upgrade against relying more heavily on Queen Elizabeth's secondary weapons.
segments.question: Should the World of Warships Queen Elizabeth use the main armament or auxiliary armament modification?
segments.answerShort: The main armament modification is preferred because her secondary battery contributes relatively little, especially against destroyers.
